title: An Artificial Intelligence (AI) Transition with No Jobless Growth
what_it_is: An Artificial Intelligence (AI) Transition with No Jobless Growth

sections.label: Singapore growth and workers compact
sections.summary: Since Independence, Singapore's growth has been anchored in a compact that workers advance as the economy advances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Since Independence, Singapore's growth has been anchored in a simple but powerful compact: as our economy advances, our workers advance together.

sections.label: Job security top concern
sections.summary: One in five NTUC survey respondents cite job security as their top concern, linked to AI and automation anxieties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: One in five respondents NTUC surveyed cite job security as their top concern, linked to anxieties around AI and automation.

sections.label: AI Centres of Excellence
sections.summary: More than 60 AI Centres of Excellence in Singapore support AI deployment across workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Today, more than 60 AI Centres of Excellence in Singapore are supporting AI deployment across workplaces.

sections.label: Singapore's desired AI outcomes
sections.summary: Singapore's desired AI outcomes are growing the economic pie, enabling enterprises and training workers, and investing in workers for AI-augmented roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As Singapore pushes ahead strategically on AI, our desired outcomes are clear: to grow our economic pie as large as possible, while ensuring that this growth translates into good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans; to enable enterprises to use AI technologies to transform and train workers to do higher-value work, take on broader roles and create more value; and to invest in our workers and empower them, preparing them early to move into AI-augmented roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Not AI instead of workers, but AI working for workers across all collars, across enterprises.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG and Tripartite Jobs Council
sections.summary: NTUC launched AI-Ready SG, and tripartite partners set up the Tripartite Jobs Council to support transformation, job redesign and worker transitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC also launched AI-Ready SG to empower more workers to use AI in their daily work, with AI-enabled tools to support jobseekers and workers of all collars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: To build further on this, tripartite partners have set up the Tripartite Jobs Council to support enterprise transformation, job redesign and worker transitions, forging win-win.

sections.label: PSA AI and SME constraints
sections.summary: At PSA, AI-enabled systems are rolled out to improve operational planning and safety, while SMEs face tighter resource constraints despite employing about 70% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: At Port of Singapore Authority (PSA), supported by the Singapore Port Workers Union and the Port Officers' Union, AI-enabled systems are progressively rolled out to improve operational planning and safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: But small and medium enterprises (SMEs) often face tighter constraints in resources, expertise and bandwidth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This matters because SMEs employ about 70% of our workforce.

sections.label: Company Training Committees formed
sections.summary: More than 3,800 Company Training Committees have been formed since 2019, benefiting over 300,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Since the first Company Training Committee in 2019, we have formed more than 3,800 Company Training Committees, with projects and training benefiting more than 300,000 blue- and white-collar workers.

sections.label: PreSAGE patient fall monitoring
sections.summary: PreSAGE is an AI-trained thermal sensor system that alerts nurses when fall-risk patients enter an unsafe fall zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: PreSAGE is a smart patient monitoring system for fall-risk patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: It uses an AI-trained system with thermal sensors above the patient's bed to capture heat patterns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: When the patient is predicted to enter an unsafe fall zone, the AI system triggers an alert to nurses to respond.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG worker training
sections.summary: Over 4,000 workers have started AI training under NTUC's AI-Ready SG, which aims for over one million training places.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Since the launch of NTUC's AI-Ready SG initiative in February, more than 4,000 workers have embarked on AI training to level up their AI skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC LearningHub intends to scale these efforts under AI-Ready SG to more than one million training places over the next few years.

sections.label: AI Transformation Blueprints partnerships
sections.summary: NTUC co-developed AI Transformation Blueprints with AI Singapore and partners with AWS and Huawei as Lead Multipliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC has co-developed AI Transformation Blueprints with AI Singapore to help companies assess their readiness, identify gaps and implement the most suitable AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We are also partnering AWS and Huawei as Lead Multipliers to bring their expertise, solutions and networks to help more enterprises and workers.

sections.label: Advance notification of retrenchments
sections.summary: The speaker calls for advance notification of retrenchments to the Government so support systems can act early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: That is why our support systems must act as early as possible and support these affected workers to bounce back on their feet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I have called in this House for advance notification of retrenchments to the Government.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme expansion
sections.summary: NTUC welcomes the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme and proposes expanding its coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: That is why financial support during transition matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We are glad that the Government has taken on board NTUC's suggestions to introduce the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement now proposes to expand the coverage of the scheme.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council on AI
sections.summary: NTUC, the Government and employers established the Tripartite Jobs Council to drive AI transformation and employment support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC, the Government and employers have established the Tripartite Jobs Council to drive AI transformation and employment support.

sections.label: Investment in education and skills
sections.summary: Singapore has invested much in education and the skills of its workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Singapore has invested much in education and the skills of our workforce.

sections.label: Four moves for AI transition
sections.summary: The four practical moves are a call for collective action in the AI transition, forming a renewed compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The four practical moves I have outlined are a call for collective action in this AI transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Act early so we understand how jobs are changing and give workers and businesses better foresight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Support enterprise transformation while uplifting workers for win-win outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: And when disruption occurs, ensure that workers bounce back with dignity and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This renewed compact must be the foundation of our unique tripartism in the AI era, keeping enterprises competitive and workers firmly at the heart of our progress.

sections.label: AI productivity gains across sectors
sections.summary: Generative AI improves customer service productivity by around 15%, with double-digit gains in software engineering and improvements in operations and supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In customer service, generative AI improves productivity by around 15%, with larger gains among less experienced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Firms are also seeing double-digit gains in software engineering while in operations and supply chains, AI is improving forecasting, reducing waste and optimising inventory and logistics.

sections.label: Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package and agency merger
sections.summary: The Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package offers advisory support and grants, while merging SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore aims to address multiple schemes and claims processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recently introduced Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) as programme partners, companies can access advisory support to redesign processes and job roles and tap on the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant for consultancy, workforce technology adoption and capability building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, today, firms are still navigating multiple schemes, multiple agencies and multiple claims processes, slowing adoption at the point where speed matters most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I am heartened to hear from Minister Tan last night that the merger of SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into Skills and Workforce Development Agency aims to solve this issue.

sections.label: Flexibility for SME AI expertise
sections.summary: For SMEs, one area to consider is giving targeted flexibility to bring in specialised AI expertise beyond existing manpower constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For SMEs, one area we can consider is to give targeted flexibility to bring in specialised AI expertise beyond existing manpower constraints.

sections.label: SCCCI AI programmes for SMEs
sections.summary: SCCCI's AI Experience and AI Enablement Programmes, with IMDA and polytechnics, help SMEs develop AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) AI Experience Programme, launched together with the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) in support of the Digital Enterprise Blueprint shows this clearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, SCCCI's AI Enablement Programme allows SMEs to define real problems and work with students from Nanyang Polytechnic, Singapore Polytechnic, Temasek Polytechnic and the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) to develop solutions.

sections.label: Place and train model
sections.summary: The passage proposes moving to a place and train model with temporary wage support to receiving employers under an industry transition fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: No worker wants to be retrenched, spend months in training and still face uncertainty about the next job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should, therefore, move more deliberately towards a "place and train" model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If another company is prepared to take in a displaced worker, even if the fit is not immediate, we should support that transition directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This can be done by targeting temporary wage support to the receiving employer, similar to the spirit of Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) but anchored under an industry transition fund so that companies are incentivised to hire first and retrain on the job.

sections.label: Building trust in AI transition
sections.summary: Trust must be built through AI deployment, job redesign and worker support, with businesses and Government enabling the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Trust must, therefore, be built deliberately through how AI is deployed, how jobs are redesigned and how workers are supported through change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We cannot say every worker matters and then leave workers to navigate this transition alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses must lead in redesigning jobs and investing in their people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And Government must ensure the system enables both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us take the proactive path to work together, to build trust early and ensure that AI expands opportunity rather than narrows it.

sections.label: NTUC survey on AI job fear
sections.summary: NTUC's yearly economic sentiments survey found fear of AI replacing jobs is more pronounced for PMETs and entry-level jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Based on the NTUC's survey on economic sentiments in Singapore, which it conducts yearly, the fear that AI would replace their job or current role is more pronounced for professionals, managers and technicians (PMETs) and entry-level jobseekers.

sections.label: Clerical roles exposed, hiring shifts
sections.summary: Routine clerical and processing roles are most exposed, while hiring shifts to data, AI, cybersecurity and governance roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Routine clerical and processing roles are most exposed, while hiring is shifting towards higher-skilled roles in data, AI, cybersecurity and governance.

sections.label: Task reconfiguration within jobs
sections.summary: Credit officers and contact centre roles are shifting tasks, showing reconfiguration of tasks within jobs rather than wholesale replacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, credit officers are moving towards interpreting and oversight while contact centre roles are shifting towards experiential, escalation and trust-building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, what we are seeing is not wholesale job replacement, but a reconfiguration of tasks within jobs.

sections.label: Industry Training Continuity Maps proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes considering Industry Training Continuity Maps alongside ITMs to sustain skilled human workers as AI takes over routine tasks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In particular, we should consider whether we need Industry Training Continuity Maps alongside our ITMs, to ensure that even as AI takes over more routine tasks, we continue to sustain a strong pipeline of deeply skilled human workers especially in roles where mastery, judgement and hands-on expertise cannot be replaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Today, this is less visible in skilled trades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is why I have also proposed a National Master Trades Accreditation framework during the last Committee of Supply, to recognise progression, reward deep skills and integrate AI competencies.

sections.label: National AI Council and Budget 2026
sections.summary: Budget 2026 announced a National AI Council led by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, plus business incentives and worker support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 announced the establishment of a National AI Council led by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, alongside incentives for businesses through the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and support for workers via SkillsFuture and the TechSkills Accelerator.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim jobseeker employment assistance
sections.summary: From 2022 to 2025, Workforce Singapore and e2i assisted over 29,000 Malay/Muslim jobseekers, placing more than 19,000 into jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Between 2022 and 2025, Workforce Singapore and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) assisted over 29,000 Malay/Muslim jobseekers, with more than 19,000 placed into jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the same time, through community-based pathways under M³ and FA4, over 6,000 jobseekers were engaged, with more than 500 securing employment, including those requiring more sustained support.

sections.label: Langkah Digital AI workshops pilot
sections.summary: MENDAKI and e2i jointly piloted Langkah Digital AI workshops in community settings for underserved Malay/Muslim workers, with plans to scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For underserved Malay/Muslim workers, as an early step, MENDAKI and NTUC's e2i jointly piloted Langkah Digital AI workshops in community settings, with plans to scale further this year; and I plan to attend some of these workshops.

sections.label: AI Bilingual accreditation for employers
sections.summary: The passage raises the possibility of launching an AI Bilingual accreditation for employers, not just workers and jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One possibility is to launch an "AI Bilingual" accreditation, for employers and not just for workers and jobseekers.

sections.label: AI uses by different workers
sections.summary: The passage gives examples of tradesmen, lower-wage workers and platform workers using AI tools for various work tasks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, tradesmen can use AI tools to generate quotations, invoices and customer responses; lower-wage workers can use AI for scheduling and financial planning; and platform workers can optimise routes and jobs across platforms, increasing autonomy.

sections.label: Growth opportunities for Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: The passage states a want for growth that creates opportunities and empowers workers, and a plan to assess economic shifts and encourage Malay/Muslim participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We want growth that creates opportunities and empowers workers, not replaces them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We will assess the implications of the economic shifts that the Economic Strategy Review Committee will outline, identify new sectors and growth opportunities and understand how we can encourage broader participation from the Malay/Muslim community in these areas.

sections.label: MENDAKI Achievement Programme AI tools
sections.summary: MENDAKI's MAP now uses AI tools like Khanmigo and KiteSense Luminee to enhance learning outcomes of less privileged students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At MENDAKI, the MENDAKI Achievement Programme, or MAP, now uses AI tools such as Khanmigo and KiteSense Luminee to enhance the learning outcomes of students from less privileged backgrounds.

sections.label: MENDAKI Langkah Digital AI workshops
sections.summary: MENDAKI's Langkah Digital initiative provides AI-Ready workshops, hands-on training and upskilling programmes to help individuals understand and apply AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, MENDAKI's Langkah Digital initiative provides AI-Ready workshops, hands-on training and upskilling programmes to help individuals understand and apply AI in their lives and work.

sections.label: AI can widen inequality
sections.summary: The passage states that if left unmanaged AI can widen inequality, and that AI must drive inclusive growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But if left unmanaged, it can widen inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must ensure that AI drives not just growth, but inclusive growth.

sections.label: Automated vehicles and autonomous buses
sections.summary: At Pasir Panjang Terminal driverless automated guided vehicles move containers, and autonomous bus services are set to run on two routes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: At Pasir Panjang Terminal, driverless automated guided vehicles move containers between yards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: And our first revenue-generating autonomous bus services are set to run on two routes in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Electric bus fleet EV training gaps
sections.summary: The passage states a move towards 50% of the bus fleet becoming electric by 2030, and that bus captains flagged gaps in EV training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Even as we move towards 50% of our bus fleet becoming electric by 2030, our bus captains flagged that EV training had important gaps.

sections.label: Bus captains' AV job worries
sections.summary: NTWU surveyed around 500 bus captains and technicians; one in three feared AVs would affect their jobs, with job security the top worry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In anticipation of our first AV bus services, NTWU, last year, surveyed around 500 bus captains and technicians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: One in three expressed concern that AVs would affect their jobs – job security was the top worry, followed by fears of pay cuts.

sections.label: Captains' figure on AV impact
sections.summary: Captains said the figure is closer to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Our captains told us it is closer to 20%.

sections.label: Workers at centre of transformation
sections.summary: Putting workers and work processes at the centre of transformation is the method, illustrated by Chye Thiam Maintenance and Grab.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Putting workers and work processes at the centre of transformation is not optional, it is the method.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It is Chye Thiam Maintenance offering $200 training allowance to workers who volunteer to be trained on their robo-sweepers, making transformation something workers choose and not something done to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It is Grab working with unions to assess whether an AV Shuttle safety driver can sustain a full eight-hour shift on continuous alert because worker welfare is part of the design and not an afterthought.

sections.label: Call for sectoral AI uplift plans
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to resource sectoral AI uplift plans for retail, logistics and healthcare with the deliberateness guiding the AV roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: But Mr Speaker, this really requires investment and intentionality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to resource sectoral AI uplift plans for industries – retail, logistics, healthcare – with the same deliberateness that has started to guide our AV roadmap for public transport.

sections.label: Conditions on AI grants
sections.summary: AI grants must be tied to mandatory job redesign and productivity gains linked to worker outcomes, with early notification of workers companies cannot retain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: AI grants must be tied to mandatory job redesign requirements and productivity gains linked to worker outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If these enterprises are unable to retain our workers, these companies should be required to notify the Government early on personnel whom they are unable to retain, so that these displaced workers can be assisted by e2i and our newly-formed Tripartite Jobs Council.

sections.label: Understanding workers not yet transitioning
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the new Skills and Workforce Development Agency will understand the needs of those not yet able to transition, who are not homogeneous.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: For those who are not yet able to make that transition, I also hope that the newly established Skills and Workforce Development Agency will take the time to understand their needs more carefully – because they are not a homogeneous group and cannot be treated as one.

sections.label: Recognition of workers' contributions
sections.summary: The speaker says these contributions have long lacked sufficient recognition and welcomes MOM's efforts starting with the electrical trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Their contributions have long gone without sufficient recognition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has begun driving efforts in this area, starting with the electrical trade.

sections.label: Employers and platform partners' role
sections.summary: Employers and platform partners must stay involved in transition support, co-sharing training cost, covering opportunity cost and supporting workers through employment pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Employers and platform partners must lean in as their business models evolve and not step back.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: This means staying involved in transition support, co-sharing training cost, covering opportunity cost and supporting workers through employment and post-employment pathways.

sections.label: Government facilitation for job redesign
sections.summary: The speaker looks to the Government to provide practical facilitation, frameworks and funding that makes job redesign achievable for companies, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Most companies, especially our SMEs, cannot do this alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I look to the Government to provide practical facilitation, frameworks and funding that makes job redesign achievable.

sections.label: Labour Movement as connective tissue
sections.summary: The Labour Movement is ready to match displaced workers to redesigned roles, advocate for fair treatment and hold everyone, including itself, to account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Our Labour Movement is ready to be the connective tissue of this transition, matching displaced workers to redesigned roles, advocating for fair treatment and holding everyone, including ourselves, to account.

sections.label: Research on AI and labour
sections.summary: A 2025 NBER paper found higher AI exposure reduces labour demand, while an MIT and Stanford study found generative AI tools boosted productivity nearly 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2025 US National Bureau of Economic Research working paper found that tasks with higher AI exposure do experience reduced labour demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, a study published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Danielle Li and Stanford's Erik Brynjolfsson found that generated AI tools boosted worker productivity by nearly 15%, with the greatest gains among the less experienced workers, thus suggesting AI can be a ladder, not just a trapdoor.

sections.label: Altman on AI and power
sections.summary: In 2021 Sam Altman predicted AI would shift power from labour to capital, and that without policy adaptation most people would be worse off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2021, OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman predicted in his blog post "Moore's Law for Everything" that AI would shift power from labour to capital, positing that if public policy does not adapt accordingly, most people will end up worse off than they are today.

sections.label: Reskilling hampered by low-utility training
sections.summary: Current reskilling efforts are hampered by low-utility external training programmes producing certifications lacking real-world currency in an AI-driven economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our current efforts to reskill Singaporeans are often hampered by the trap of low-utility external training programmes which produce certifications that lack real-world currency in an AI-driven economy.

sections.label: Proposed National AI Equity Fund
sections.summary: The speaker proposes establishing a National AI Equity Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address this, I propose the establishment of a National AI Equity Fund.

sections.label: Social dividend for adult citizens
sections.summary: A social dividend would pay every adult Singapore citizen $500 initially, costing about $1.5 billion annually, scaling as fund contributions grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first is a social dividend where revenue is distributed as a direct payout to every adult Singapore citizen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose an initial citizen dividend of $500 per adult citizen, scaling upward as fund contributions grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on our current citizen population, this would cost approximately $1.5 billion annually – or less than 10% of last year's Budget surplus – and provide a meaningful return to every Singaporean household.

sections.label: Mastery fund for on-the-job training
sections.summary: A mastery fund would provide an employer-led OJT model with a mastery apprentice wage covering 50% of gross salary, capped at median wage for six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The other portion of the fund will be dedicated to a mastery fund, which will be an employer-led, on-the-job training (OJT) model that moves training out of the classroom and into every enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose that the mastery fund provides a mastery apprentice wage covering 50% of the gross salary, capped at a median wage for six months, for any Singapore citizen entering or transitioning into an AI-augmented role.

sections.label: Corporate income tax increase
sections.summary: The first source is a two percentage point increase in corporate income tax for firms with annual profits exceeding $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first source is a marginal increase of two percentage points of the corporate income tax rate for firms with annual profits exceeding $100 million.

sections.label: Raising net investment returns
sections.summary: The second source raises the maximum net investment returns taken into the Budget from 50% to 52.5%, with the additional 2.5% flowing into the fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second source is a targeted increase in the utilisation of our investment returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose raising the maximum net investment returns taken into the Budget from 50% to 52.5%, with this additional 2.5% flowing directly into the fund.

sections.label: Youth Wage Credit and AI Fund
sections.summary: A Youth Wage Credit Scheme was proposed, and the National AI Equity Fund extends that logic to a framework for Singaporeans facing AI transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During this year's Committee of Supply Debate, I proposed a Youth Wage Credit Scheme – a targeted wage subsidy for employers who hire younger Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The National AI Equity Fund extends that logic into a broader longer-term framework for all Singaporeans navigating the AI transition and other technological disruptions.

sections.label: Social Dividend and Mastery Fund
sections.summary: Establishing the social dividend and mastery fund gives every Singaporean a stake in digital prosperity and resources to stay ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By establishing the social dividend and the mastery fund, we give every Singaporean a direct stake in our digital prosperity and the resources to stay ahead of the curve.

sections.label: Superaged Society and Human Resource
sections.summary: Singapore is superaged with a fertility rate of 0.87, making human resource the key bottleneck and cost driver for businesses, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We used to say that people are Singapore’s only resource.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We are now a superaged society with a total fertility rate of 0.87.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Human resource is now the key bottleneck and cost driver for most businesses, especially SMEs which are hiring 70% of local workforce.

sections.label: Talent Shortage and AI Robots
sections.summary: A survey shows most Asia Pacific employers struggle to find skilled talent, and AI-powered robots are needed to replace foreign workers in unwanted roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The 2025 ManpowerGroup's latest Talent Shortage Survey reveals that nearly four in five employers in the Asia Pacific region are struggling to find skilled talent, with 77% reporting difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: But there is a limit to our dependence on foreign workers, including political and social constraints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We need AI-powered robots to replace foreign workers in roles that no Singaporeans would want to do or can do.

sections.label: AI Transition Without Social Baggage
sections.summary: Robots carry no social baggage, and the AI transition should focus on customising physical generative AI solutions for industries to empower Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: And robots also do not carry any social baggage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I feel strongly that our AI transition should be focused on customising physical generative AI solutions for our industries, so as to help every Singaporean on this journey of empowerment.

sections.label: Union, MOM, MOE, MTI Measures
sections.summary: Unions should forecast at-risk jobs, MOM fund retraining, MOE and IHLs redesign programmes, and MTI attract physical generative AI companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: One, unions should forecast which are the types of jobs and sectors at risk, as well as numbers of workers that may be displaced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Two, MOM should fund retraining for affected workers, to prepare them for other roles or other industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Four, the Ministry of Education (MOE) and IHLs should redesign academic programmes to shift students away from fields already taken over by AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Five, the Ministry of Trade and Industry should attract more world-class physical generative AI companies to set up headquarters in Singapore and attract talents for research and development (R&D).

sections.label: Government support for AI transition
sections.summary: Government support and regulation are needed to fund retraining, create higher value jobs, attract AI firms and ensure ethical AI use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: To support this transition, Government support and regulation are crucial to fund retraining of workers, create higher value jobs, attract leading AI firms and ensure that AI is used ethically for broad societal benefit. : In the near future, a new AI ecosystem will emerge.

sections.label: Jobseeker Support payout and ceiling
sections.summary: The scheme pays up to $6,000 over six months in tapering instalments, only for workers earning $5,000 or less before redundancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As currently configured, it pays up to $6,000 over six months in tapering monthly instalments, starting at $1,500 and ending at $750 over the last three months and it is only available to workers who earn $5,000 a month or less before they were made redundant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Labour Chief acknowledged in this Chamber yesterday that the ceiling excludes PMEs who face the same displacement risk in the AI era and has proposed raising the qualifying ceiling to closer to the PME median gross income level.

sections.label: Retrenched PMETs unemployment figures
sections.summary: Of retrenched residents last quarter, 43.6% of PMETs lacked new employment within six months, and four in ten rehired earned less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of retrenched residents in the final quarter of last year, 43.6% of PMETs had not found new employment within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That is the cohort that the Jobseeker Support scheme runs out on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And of those who do find work within six months, roughly four in 10 return at lower wages than before.

sections.label: Raising ceiling widens cohort
sections.summary: Raising the ceiling widens the cohort but does not shorten the countdown, and payouts are 40% of last drawn salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Raising the ceiling only widens the cohort, but it does not shorten the countdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We pay out 40% of last drawn salary with no income ceiling and no tapering mechanism.

sections.label: Retraining tax credit proposal
sections.summary: A retraining tax credit was proposed, available only to firms that retained an existing worker into an AI-augmented role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In February, in this House, I propose a retraining tax credit, a deduction available only to firms that can demonstrate that they have retained an existing worker into an AI-augmented role, rather than retrenching them.

sections.label: National AI Equity Fund proposal
sections.summary: Gerald Giam proposed a National AI Equity Fund to deliver on that commitment structurally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My colleague Gerald Giam has proposed a National AI Equity Fund to deliver on that commitment structurally.

sections.label: Annual AI gains audit proposal
sections.summary: The Government is investing public money in four national AI mission sectors, and the speaker asks for an annual AI gains audit reporting to Parliament on how productivity gains are distributed between wages and returns to capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government is investing serious public money at scale in four national AI mission sectors, advanced manufacturing connectivity, finance and healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These are appropriate investments, but public investment creates a corresponding public accountability obligation. where public money goes in, the public has a right to know what is coming out and to whom.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, what I am asking for is a targeted transparency mechanism, an annual AI gains audit scoped specifically to the four national AI missions to start, reporting to Parliament on how productivity gains from state-backed AI investments are being distributed between wages and returns to capital.

sections.label: No mechanism to track gains
sections.summary: The tax code says nothing at the fork between retraining and retaining workers, and no mechanism exists to tell whether gains from public AI investment reach the intended people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our tax code says nothing to affirm at the fork between retraining workers and retaining them and we have built no mechanism to tell whether the gains from public AI investment are reaching the people whose name that investment has been made.

sections.label: PM Wong on protecting workers
sections.summary: Prime Minister Wong spoke about protecting every worker and scaling practical tripartite tools, like the CTCs for the AI transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Wong spoke about protecting every worker and scaling practical tripartite tools, like the CTCs for the AI transition.

sections.label: Clearer AI-relevant training pathways
sections.summary: The speaker suggests curating clearer AI-relevant pathways by sector and job role, with a clear front door and employer recognition, and considering incentives for priority courses with clear employer demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: A worker should not need to scroll for hours to guess what really matters to him or his next job.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: So, I suggest that we curate clearer AI-relevant pathways by sector, by job role, with a clear front door and clear employer recognition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And we can consider additional incentives for those who choose priority courses that support AI-enabled growth, especially when there is clear employer demand.

sections.label: HSEU and GP+ AI training agreement
sections.summary: HSEU and GP+ Co-operative signed an agreement to train primary care clinic staff in AI awareness and help clinics adopt technology and redesign workflows, supported by the CTC approach and CTC Grants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In April this year, HSEU and GP+ Co-operative signed an agreement to train primary care clinic staff in AI awareness, and to help primary care clinics adopt technology and redesign their workflows, supported by the CTC approach and the CTC Grants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The value is in making adoption practical, responsible and anchored on job redesign, and not just a tool roll-out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that we can extend this cluster-based, CTC-style approach to other professional sectors too, including law and accountancy, so smaller practices can move from uncertainty to readiness, with clear governance standards and worker protection.

sections.label: Growth with worker support
sections.summary: The passage states that growth must bring employment opportunities and support for change, and that the test is whether a worker can quickly see the right course, for the right job, at the right time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: When growth comes, employment opportunities must come with it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Support for change must also come with it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Growth that workers can feel, in wages, in dignity, in a clear next step.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The test is whether a worker can quickly see the right course, for the right job, at the right time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If we keep this direction and refine delivery with tripartite resolve, Singapore can deploy AI effectively, responsibly and at speed, while strengthening trust and protecting dignity.

sections.label: Singapore workforce AI exposure
sections.summary: Singapore is highly vulnerable to AI disruption, with IMF estimates that about 77% of its local workforce is highly exposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore is one of the most vulnerable economies to AI disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Because we are a high-skill services-oriented hub, estimates from the IMF indicate that approximately 77% of our local workforce is highly exposed to AI disruption, and our transition is likely to be sharper and more acute than in many other economies.

sections.label: Clerical and administrative job risk
sections.summary: Clerical support workers and many business and administrative associate professionals face the highest risk that their roles will shrink or disappear.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clerical support workers and many business and administrative associate professionals, whose work is built around routine documentation, basic processing and standardised customer queries, face the highest risk that their roles will shrink or even disappear.

sections.label: High-end jobs create local jobs
sections.summary: Studies from major tech hubs including San Francisco indicate each high-end job is associated with about four local service-sector jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Studies from major tech hubs, including San Francisco, indicate that each high-end job is associated with the creation of approximately four jobs in local service sectors, such as retail and food services.

sections.label: AI and income inequality
sections.summary: The IMF and World Bank have noted AI could exacerbate income inequality without policy intervention.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: International institutions, including the IMF and World Bank, have noted that AI could exacerbate income inequality in the absence of policy intervention.

sections.label: Women in AI-intensive STEM roles
sections.summary: A 2024 IMF report found women under-represented in AI-intensive STEM roles and among workers with AI engineering skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2024 IMF report on Singapore's labour market found that women are under-represented in AI-intensive science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) roles, and among workers with AI engineering skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Women in STEM held 29% of entry-level positions, 24.4% of managerial positions but only 12.12% of C-suite roles.

sections.label: Women-dominated occupations GenAI exposure
sections.summary: ILO data released in March 2026 found women-dominated occupations nearly twice as likely to be exposed to GenAI risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, International Labour Organization data, released in March 2026, found that occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to GenAI risks compared with male-dominated ones, with even stronger differences presenting when looking at high automation risk.

sections.label: Graduate employment anxiety 2025
sections.summary: Over 20% of 2025 graduates lack full-time permanent roles, a nearly 5% rise from 2023, and over 60% find job search difficult.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With more than 20% of graduates unable to secure full-time permanent roles in 2025, a nearly 5% increase from 2023, and over 60% of graduates claiming that the job search has become difficult, it is only natural that young graduates have become more anxious about landing full-time employment.

sections.label: AI apprenticeship programme indicators
sections.summary: The AI apprenticeship programme is assessed through three indicators: practitioners trained, graduates in AI engineering roles, and project quality completion and supervision.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Following up in response to my Parliamentary Question on 24 February this year, I noted that the AI apprenticeship programme is currently assessed through three primary indicators: one, the total number of practitioners trained; two, the percentage of AI Apprenticeship Programme graduates who took up AI engineering related roles, and; three, the completion and supervision of project quality.

sections.label: AI startup support and grants
sections.summary: AI reduces business barriers, but existing startup schemes may not provide sustained long-term support, and grant architecture remains milestone heavy and programme bound.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: AI has greatly reduced barriers to starting a business by being deployed to build websites, analyse data, run marketing and even automate back-office tasks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have many schemes for startups, such as grants and boot camps, but do these initiatives adequately provide sustained long-term support across the full lifecycle of a burgeoning firm?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, our grant architecture remains milestone heavy and programme bound, encouraging compliance over competition.

sections.label: Singapore ecosystem collaboration policy-driven
sections.summary: Despite anchors like Grab and Block 71, the Asian Development Bank noted Singapore's ecosystem trails others because collaboration remains policy-driven rather than organically clustered.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While we have anchors like Grab and Block 71, the Asian Development Bank has noted that our ecosystem trails others because our collaboration remains policy-driven rather than organically clustered.

sections.label: OECD study Singapore student failure fear
sections.summary: A 2018 OECD study found Singapore students expressed greater fear of failure than peers in any other participating country.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2018 piece of study by the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) found that Singapore students expressed a greater fear of failure than their peers compared with any other participating country.

sections.label: Failed founders bankruptcy restrictions
sections.summary: Founders who fail face the same restrictions as other bankrupts, including travel bans, director disqualification and no automatic discharge, regardless of cause.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, founders who fail face the same restrictions as any other bankrupt, with travel bans, director disqualification and no automatic discharge, regardless of whether their failure was the result of genuine risk-taking or financial misconduct.

sections.label: High income countries AI dominance
sections.summary: World Bank 2025 data show high income countries account for most notable AI models, AI startups and venture capital funding despite 17% of global population.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: World Bank 2025 data show that high income countries account for 87% of notable AI models, 86% of AI startups and 91% of venture fund capital funding, despite representing just 17% of the global population.

sections.label: Equitable AI access in ASEAN
sections.summary: Singapore has begun developing Southeast Asian language AI tools through Project Sea Lion and should champion equitable AI access across ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Recently, we have already begun developing AI tools tailored to Southeast Asian languages through Project Sea Lion, recognising that much of the developing world risks being left behind by AI systems built on Western data.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should build on this by championing equitable AI access across the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), exporting our governance expertise to nations that lack the capacity to develop their own frameworks and ensuring that the rules governing AI reflect not just the interests of the powerful, but the needs of the many.

sections.label: Singapore's global AI leadership leverage
sections.summary: Singapore's standing in the global AI ecosystem gives leverage to shape AI development and adoption, creating jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore's standing in the global AI ecosystem, gives us leverage to shape how AI tools are built, deployed and adopted across the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: When our researchers develop AI system that work across Southeast Asian languages, we create tools that can be deployed in our own service sectors, our hospitals, our schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: When our companies lead in AI adoption, we generate demand for new skills, new roles and new industries that our workers can be trained into.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: We must ensure Singaporeans are in the room where these technologies are being built and not merely be on the receiving end of decisions made elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Our global AI leadership is ultimately an investment in ensuring that the answer is the former.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: This approach also ultimately has the added benefit of creating more jobs and opportunities for Singapore in what would be a true trickle-down effect.

sections.label: Enterprise AI adoption deliberate thread
sections.summary: Enterprise AI adoption must follow a deliberate thread: build AI fluency, drive workflow and job redesign, and ensure shared outcomes for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To achieve growth without casualties, enterprise AI adoption cannot just be about buying technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It must follow a deliberate thread: we must first build AI fluency; use that fluency to drive workflow and job redesign; and ensure that this redesign leads to tangible, shared outcomes for our workers.

sections.label: Fragmented AI literacy bottleneck
sections.summary: In AI Fluency workshops with over 20 Temasek portfolio companies, fragmented AI literacy remains a primary bottleneck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In our AI Fluency workshops with over 20 Temasek portfolio companies, we see clearly that fragmented AI literacy remains a primary bottleneck.

sections.label: Conditionalities for public support schemes
sections.summary: The Government is asked to establish clear conditionalities and a scorecard for support schemes tracking net new roles, workflow redesign, wages, retention and upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ensure public funds do not subsidise this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I ask the Government: can we establish clear conditionalities for our support schemes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A scorecard that tracks the number of net new roles created, the scale of workflow redesign, wage improvements, staff retention and upskilling.

sections.label: Supporting businesses with retraining costs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry how companies can be better supported to absorb short-term lags so retraining time does not become an excuse for lay-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, we must acknowledge that many businesses struggling with high operating costs in this challenging economy do not have the luxury of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask the Ministry: how can we better support companies to absorb these short-term lags, ensuring that the cost of time required to retrain workers does not become an excuse for lay-offs?

sections.label: AI tools in broken workflows
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government and tripartite partners whether support schemes can be expanded to explicitly look into workflow redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Workers resist change not because they are stubborn but because it is deeply frustrating to use advanced AI tools within broken workflows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, I ask the Government and our tripartite partners: can we expand our support schemes to explicitly look into workflow redesign?

sections.label: Tracking AI disruption safety nets
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government how it tracks the speed and effectiveness of existing measures, particularly the financial runway for displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The answer is that AI disruption moves at an unprecedented speed and workers worry our safety nets cannot catch them fast enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask the Government: how are we rigorously tracking the speed and effectiveness of our existing measures, particularly the financial runway for displaced workers, to guarantee that they remain truly responsive?

sections.label: Protecting entry-level pathways for youth
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government how it works with employers and industry leaders to protect and redesign entry-level pathways for youth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If young graduates cannot get a real first job and the mentorship they need, they will never gain the foundational experience earlier cohorts relied on to grow and we risk losing our future workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask the Government: how are we working with employers and industry leaders to protect and redesign entry-level pathways so that our youth can develop the professional judgment required to become the AI conductors of tomorrow?

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council establishment
sections.summary: The passage states that establishing the Tripartite Jobs Council is an important step in ensuring alignment happens in practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The establishment of the Tripartite Jobs Council is an important step in ensuring that this alignment happens in practice.

sections.label: AI displacement and hiring slowdown
sections.summary: The passage states that job displacement of current workers due to AI has been modest and localised, while the hiring slowdown of new workers is evident and likely to accelerate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The evidence shows that to date, job displacement of current workers due to AI has been modest and localised whereas the hiring slowdown of new workers is already evident and even likely to accelerate.

sections.label: Retrenchments and PMET unemployment
sections.summary: MOM's labour market report shows retrenchments stable since 2023 and unemployment about 2%, with 960 PMET retrenchments in AI-exposed sectors in the last quarter.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MOM's latest labour market report reveals that since 2023, overall retrenchments have remained stable and the unemployment rate of about 2% has not budged much since 2022.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to questions about the PMET sector, Senior Parliamentary Secretary for Manpower Shawn Huang also pointed out that retrenchments among PMETs in AI-exposed sectors such as finance and infocomm remain low, numbering only 960 in the final quarter of last year.

sections.label: Graduate employment survey decline
sections.summary: The graduate employment survey shows a drop in job placement across almost every field, with about one in four graduates lacking full-time employment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The latest graduate employment survey shows a drop in the share of graduates that managed to land a job in almost every single field of study, with around one in every four graduates unable to secure full-time employment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on my calculations, what is true that pre-pandemic and permanent employment among graduates averaged around 70% in 2020, it was closer to 85% as recently as a decade ago, which is significantly better.

sections.label: Overqualification among early-career workers
sections.summary: Overqualification is greatest for those early in their careers, and the gap between involuntary and voluntary underemployment is greatest for those under 30.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Overqualification is the greatest for those who are early in their careers and the gap between the involuntary and voluntarily underemployed is greatest for those under 30.

sections.label: Expanding GRIT programme nationally
sections.summary: The speaker calls for expanding the existing GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) programme into a national, cross-sectoral internship initiative.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As I have shared in the long cut for this year's Committee of Supply, this would call for expanding the existing GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) programme to a national level, cross-sectoral national internship initiative.

sections.label: Apprenticeship employment pathways and protections
sections.summary: Short-term apprenticeships and internships should embed a clear employment pathway and trainees should be treated as employees under the Employment Act with the same protections.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, such short term, by which I mean six months to a year, apprenticeships and internships should also embed a clear employment pathway, conditional on reasonable performance on the part of the employee, unless a waiver is granted to employers due to changed economic circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These trainees should be treated as employees under the Employment Act and receive the same legal protections and entitlements, including a minimum period of annual leave, which GRIT trainees currently do not receive.

sections.label: Ending public sector diploma requirements
sections.summary: The speaker urges ending public sector hiring requirements for a diploma or degree if the competency can be demonstrated otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fourth, if indeed we stand by our belief that we want our graduates to focus on acquiring competencies rather than certifications, as MOE has made clear in its support for stackable, micro-credentials pathways in our autonomous universities and as corroborated by recent research, then we should put our money where our mouth is and end hiring requirements that insist on a diploma or degree in the public sector if the competency can be demonstrated, otherwise.

sections.label: Agents working 24/7 productivity
sections.summary: A person with agents working 24/7 said he performed the task of five persons compared with last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the broadband was down, they came back to check on their agents to see are they really working?" So, I asked, "How would you know they are really working?" The answer, "Well, actually, they produce the code at any time, all the way, 24/7." So, he has got agents, they are working 24/7.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I said, "How do you measure the productivity?" And I asked one question, "How many tasks or jobs have you replaced since, or how many jobs have you done, the capabilities of people doing the engineers or the coding jobs, since last year, one year ago?" And the answer that came back is five.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, compared with last year and this year, this guy has agents working for him and he performed the task of five persons.

sections.label: Worker two years behind technology
sections.summary: Asked if he was up to par, the answer was that he is two years behind current technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is he up to par?" And the answer that came back is, "Well, based on what I discussed with him and his answer shows he is two years behind the current technology".

sections.label: SWDA defining workplace competencies
sections.summary: The new agency SWDA should work with the Labour Movement to define competencies, possibly involving professional institutions for certified, recognised micro-credentials.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where are the competencies level at the workplace?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I think the new agency, SWDA, should be able to work together with the Labour Movement to define the competencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it fixed to workplaces; so, one workplace, one company?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, maybe we can consider involving the professional institutions, so that for each level or each competency level, whether it is stackable, micro-credentials, they are all certified and recognised by the industry.

sections.label: Legislative force for flexible work
sections.summary: The speaker proposes upgrading the Flexible Work Arrangement Guidelines to legislative force so employees can enjoy AI productivity gains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At present, when technology is adopted to improve productivity, it is often the employer who benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I propose upgrading the Flexible Work Arrangement Guidelines so they are given legislative force, which ensures that employees too, can enjoy AI productivity gains.

sections.label: Tracking AI impact on students
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to track and report on AI adoption's impact on students' cognitive development across age groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Children in their formative years should be learning how to think, ask questions and making judgements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to track and regularly report on the impact that AI adoption in our schools has on the cognitive development of students across different age groups.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements legislative force
sections.summary: During the MOM Committee of Supply debate in March, the speaker made a case for flexible work arrangements to be given legislative force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: During the MOM Committee of Supply debate in March, I made a case for flexible work arrangements to be given legislative force.

sections.label: Worker well-being and AI policy
sections.summary: It means fewer caregivers choosing between job and family, and rest, in a country where 61% of employees feel exhausted and 39% dread work, asking if Government will prioritise worker well-being alongside employer gains and growth in AI era policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It means fewer caregivers having to choose between a job and a family member who needs them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It also means rest, real rest, in a country where 61% of employees feel exhausted and 39% of workers dread going to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government and tripartite movement commit to prioritising worker well-being alongside employer gains and economic growth as it shapes AI era policy?

sections.label: Brookings study on AI in education
sections.summary: A January Brookings Institution global study found the biggest risk of AI in education is displacement of effortful thinking during development years, with 65% of surveyed students citing undermined cognitive development as the top risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A global study published this January by the Brookings Institution found that the biggest risk of AI in education is the displacement of effortful thinking during crucial development years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Interestingly, 65% of the students surveyed in this study cited the undermining of cognitive development as the top risk of the use of AI.

sections.label: Children's AI use and development
sections.summary: It says technology speed should not outpace care for children, welcomes SG LEADS expansion to study Singapore children's AI usage patterns and effects on learning and well-being, and hopes it covers cognitive development impacts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should not let the speed of a technology cycle outpace the care that our children deserve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I also appreciate the Minister's update this morning that the Singapore Longitudinal Early Development Study (SG LEADS) by A*STAR will expand to collect data that will help us understand Singapore children's AI usage patterns and how AI usage affects their learning and well-being outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope this will also include the impact of using AI tools in education on our children's cognitive development, including their effect on their executive function and skills like critical thinking, reading comprehension and capacity for sustained independent effort.

sections.label: Right to flexible work
sections.summary: For today's workers, the right to flexible work should be legislated so productivity gains are reclaimed as time for rest, care and connection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For the workers of today, we should legislate the right to flexible work so that productivity gains are reclaimed as time for rest, care and connection.

sections.label: AI workplace regulation examples
sections.summary: The EU AI Act classifies employment AI systems as high risk subject to bias testing, transparency and human oversight, complementing GDPR Article 22, while New York City's law requires bias audits and applicant notification for hiring AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For instance, in the European Union, the recently adopted Artificial Intelligence Act recognises that AI systems used in employment, such as those involved in hiring, evaluation and performance monitoring, can significantly affect workers' livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These systems are therefore classified as "high risk" and are subject to requirements such as bias testing, transparency disclosures and human oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This complements Article 22 of the General Data Protection Regulation, under which individuals have the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing where such decisions produce legal effects concerning him or her or significantly affect him or her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In New York City, the Automated Employment Decision Tools Law requires that AI systems used in hiring or promotion undergo regular bias audits and that applicants are informed when such tools are being used.

sections.label: Displacement-exposed roles
sections.summary: As a result, roles in areas such as administrative work and those involving entry-level analysis are more exposed to displacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As a result, roles in areas such as administrative work and those involving entry-level analysis are more exposed to displacement.

sections.label: AI redeployment and creative copyright
sections.summary: Employers adopting AI can be encouraged to redeploy workers through training and job redesign, while legislation or a government framework could protect copyrighted material used to train AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In practical terms, employers adopting AI can be encouraged to identify adjacent roles for affected workers early on and to provide structured pathways for redeployment into these roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This may include short, focused training modules or job redesign which allow workers to gradually build new competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Such measures help ensure that workers are not abruptly displaced, but are instead guided through a managed transition where their skills and roles within their organisations are preserved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to the creative industries, including music, writing and acting, we should consider if legislation or further protection is needed in relation to copyrighted material being used to train AI and whether remedies for this should be purely private or whether there is scope for the Government to provide a framework for such materials to be protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If left purely to private law, only the well resourced would be able to take up the matter, whereas if there is a framework for this, individual artistes, writers and others might be able to benefit from such protection.

sections.label: Managing AI's power shift
sections.summary: The rise of AI, if not managed properly, could recalibrate power between labour and capital, as shown by Meta recording US employees' keystrokes and workflows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is growth without losing who we are as humans and as Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are extremely important goals, because if the rise of AI is not managed properly, it could represent not just technological disruption but a recalibration of power between labour and capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, last month, Meta announced that the keystrokes and workflows of every one of its employees in the US will be recorded.

sections.label: Worker protection frameworks
sections.summary: Frameworks for worker protection need strengthening in areas such as retention benefits and workers' rights over data they create at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, we need to strengthen frameworks for worker protection in areas such as retention benefits and the rights of workers over data they create at the workplace.

sections.label: Raising blue-collar wages
sections.summary: As generative AI threatens well-paying white-collar cognitive roles, wages and career pathways must be raised in blue-collar sectors that are less vulnerable to AI displacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In many other first world societies, the job of a plumber, garbage collector or an air-conditioning technician pay high enough to allow a middle-class lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We have made a policy choice to fill these roles with lower-paid foreign workers while our local workers are channelled into high-paying white-collar jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While this has worked well for us for decades, this may no longer be sustainable as generative AI threatens to reduce the number of well-paying white-collar cognitive roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must therefore raise wages and improve career pathways in blue-collar sectors that are currently less attractive and yet also less vulnerable to displacement by AI.

sections.label: Students, AI and intellectual independence
sections.summary: Outsourcing tasks to AI may erode students' capacity for creativity, imagination, judgement and empathy, or let these practical skills atrophy from lack of use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In encouraging our students to leverage AI, how can we ensure that they can continue to learn how to grapple with ideas, how to formulate arguments, how to problem solve and how to cultivate intellectual independence?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
