sentences.text: By constantly outsourcing our tasks to AI, we may erode or undermine our capacity for creativity, imagination, judgement and even empathy, or let these practical skills atrophy from lack of use.

sections.label: Human judgement not surrendered
sections.summary: Making judgements about the world and what should be done is a distinctively human task that should not be easily surrendered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Making judgements about the world and what should be done is a distinctively human task that should not be easily surrendered.

sections.label: AI-generated pantuns versus learning
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether teaching students to use AI to generate pantuns loses something valuable compared with experimenting with the lines themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In short, the pantun embodies a tradition – connecting the Malays today to our forefathers before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I want to ask: do we lose something valuable if we teach students to use AI to generate pantuns, rather than discovering the fun of experimenting with the lines themselves?

sections.label: AI and Malay cultural tradition
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether AI pantun skills translate into craft and aesthetic sensibility, and warns against an AI-centric gaze.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More importantly, does the skill of using AI to generate pantuns necessarily translate into the craft of writing a good pantun or even the aesthetic sensibility to appreciate the art form?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And what is the long-term impact to the Malay language, culture and tradition when a cultural motif is reduced to an AI output?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must be clear-sighted about what AI can and cannot offer and always ask what is the purpose AI is serving and whether it is fit for that purpose?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must avoid being boxed in into an AI-centric gaze in which we are left with a narrow and artificially mediated understanding of reality and an impoverished capacity to make sense of and relate to the world and those around us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Order, we have been in the Chambers for close to five hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.10 pm.

sections.label: Universal premium AI access
sections.summary: The speaker states that access to premium AI, especially AI agents, must be universal, not gated by course enrolment or union membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, that access to premium AI, especially AI agents, must be universal, not gated by course enrolment or union membership.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Premium AI Access Scheme
sections.summary: The Government has partially adopted Gerald Giam's 2024 suggestions through the SkillsFuture Premium AI Access Scheme, which the speaker says is gated behind course enrolment and union membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has partially adopted the 2024 suggestions of my colleague Gerald Giam to provide universal premium AI model access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Premium AI Access Scheme, six months of free tools for Singaporeans who enrol in selected courses, is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are good starts, but they are unnecessarily gated behind course enrolment and union membership.

sections.label: Premium AI as universal entitlement
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will make premium AI access a universal entitlement rather than gate it behind course completion or union membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government make premium AI access a universal entitlement, rather than gate it behind course completion or union membership?

sections.label: Bulk licensing for frontier AI
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore should seek bulk licensing agreements for agent-tier access if frontier AI agent costs rise, accepting higher national expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the possible future where frontier AI agent costs go up, not down, Singapore should seek bulk licensing agreements for agent-tier access the same way we negotiate energy supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This means accepting that frontier AI access may be a permanently higher line item in the national expenditure and procuring it systematically, because the alternative – citizens priced out of the tools that define productivity – is worse.

sections.label: Retrenchment and PMET incidence figures
sections.summary: MOM's fourth quarter 2025 report recorded about 14,490 retrenchments in 2025, up from about 13,000, with PMET incidence at 10.1 per 1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOM's own fourth quarter of 2025 Labour Market Report reported about 14,490 retrenchments in 2025, up from about 13,000 the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: PMET retrenchment incidence reached 10.1 per 1,000 resident employees, above the pre-recessionary norm of 8.0 set during 2015 to 2019.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council announced
sections.summary: The Government announced the Tripartite Jobs Council on 30 April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government announced the Tripartite Jobs Council on 30 April.

sections.label: AI transition notice and redeployment proposals
sections.summary: Proposals include a 90-day mandatory transition notice, redeployment-first obligation, and ability to challenge termination reasons, with David Shor's polling cited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, a 90-day mandatory transition notice before AI-driven role elimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, a re-deployment-first obligation, retraining or reassignment before AI-driven termination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, for workers to be able to substantively challenge the reasons for their termination if they feel they are misleading, so that these AI restructuring protections will be real.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The American pollster David Shor polled Americans this year: three to one, across every political persuasion, they chose job creation over direct transfers.

sections.label: Strategic engagement and retrenchment framework
sections.summary: It calls for strategic engagement and a retrenchment framework where the automating company bears the cost before the worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Strategic engagement, so we are not price-takers in our own future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And a retrenchment framework where the company that decides to automate bears the cost of that decision before the worker does.

sections.label: DBS reducing contract and temporary staff
sections.summary: DBS Bank announced plans to reduce its contract and temporary staff by around 4,000 across various markets, with AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Closer to home, DBS Bank has announced plans to reduce its contract and temporary staff by around 4,000 across various markets, with AI adoption.

sections.label: Arbitration rulings and human transition standard
sections.summary: Arbitration panels ruled AI replacement was not valid grounds for dismissal and a role and salary reduction was not reasonable re-assignment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In one case, the arbitration panel clarified that AI replacement was not valid grounds for dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In another case, a massive role and salary reduction due to AI taking over the work was not considered a reasonable re-assignment proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, companies must be held to a human transition standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When a company deploys AI that eliminates roles, it should be required to have a transition plan, re-deployment offers, funded retraining, phased timelines.

sections.label: PMET retrenchment and unemployment
sections.summary: It can mean prolonged unemployment, income loss and long-term repercussions, with MOM data showing a rise in PMET retrenchments compared to 2019 pre-recession norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It can mean prolonged unemployment, income loss and long-term repercussions for their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And this we are already seeing in the data that is provided by MOM, where there has been a rise in PMET retrenchments compared to the pre-recession norms in 2019, reflecting their greater exposure to sectors undergoing restructuring.

sections.label: SBS Transit AI bus maintenance
sections.summary: SBS Transit overhauled bus maintenance using AI with union and CTC Grant support, creating a diagnostic expert career scheme for over 50 workers instead of cutting jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SBS Transit, with support from the National Transport Workers Union and the CTC Grant, overhauled its bus maintenance operations using AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The company implemented AI-powered diagnostic systems for predictive maintenance and instead of cutting jobs, it created a new diagnostic expert career scheme for over 50 workers.

sections.label: NTUC AI skills partnerships
sections.summary: NTUC is partnering AWS and Huawei to equip 100,000 workers and 100 enterprises with AI skills, with union members able to tap support for up to half of AI model subscription fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More recently, NTUC is partnering global technology leaders, like Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Huawei, to equip 100,000 workers and 100 enterprises with AI skills through the CTC ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the individual level, union members can also tap on union support for up to half of the subscription fees for AI models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is in addition to the six-month subscription provided through the Government.

sections.label: Tripartite partnership protecting workers
sections.summary: The tripartite partnership between NTUC, Singapore National Employees Federation and the Government is unique, with unions protecting jobs and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: From my enterprise experience, our tripartite partnership between the NTUC, Singapore National Employees Federation and the Government is unique, so unique that many of my overseas colleagues are genuinely puzzled by how well it works with real positive outcomes for all, because our unions do not just protect jobs, they protect workers.

sections.label: AI as individual force multiplier
sections.summary: At the individual level, AI is a force multiplier that enhances productivity, augments skills and allows each worker to do more, better and faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: At the level of the individual, AI is a force multiplier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It enhances productivity, augment skills and allows each worker to do more, do better and do faster.

sections.label: Government support for AI adoption
sections.summary: The Government must provide support structures, skills frameworks, training pathways and technology access, with NTUC subsidising AI subscriptions so AI does not become a tool only for the privileged few.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And the Government must provide the support structure, strong skills framework, accessible training pathways and broad-based access to technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: That is why I am encouraged by the support the Government is providing to help Singaporeans adopt AI tools, further strengthened by NTUC's initiative to subsidise AI subscription to its members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is important because AI cannot become a tool only for the privileged few.

sections.label: Worker upskilling and job redesign
sections.summary: Enterprise and industry transformation must go with business process re-engineering and job redesign, supported by tax incentives and worker transition schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In a tight labour market, like Singapore, this enterprise and industry transformation must go hand in hand with deep business process re-engineering and meaningful job redesign, as mentioned by a few of the Members here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The real driver is how we upskill and reskill our workers so that they can take on higher value-added jobs that are increasing in demand and the opportunity cost of not doing so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The tax incentives help companies invest in the necessary AI tools and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But equally important are the schemes that support workers through this transition, whether it is programmes such as the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant, NTUC CTC Grant, the Union Training Assistance Programme, and Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes, these initiatives support job redesign, training and even provide wage support while workers undergo upskilling and reskilling.

sections.label: Risk of jobless growth
sections.summary: If workers are not ready and skills do not keep pace, Singapore risks jobless growth from a mismatch between jobs and workforce skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Because growth will come and new roles will emerge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But if our workers are not ready, if skills are not kept in pace, we risk a different kind of jobless growth – not a lack of jobs, but a mismatch between jobs and the skills our workforce has.

sections.label: Continuous reskilling and upskilling
sections.summary: Workers must continuously upgrade themselves and use support from Workforce Singapore, NTUC or community initiatives such as M3+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: That is why we must be prepared to continuously upgrade ourselves – to reskill and upskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is where it is important for us to make use of the support available – whether through Workforce Singapore (WSG) programmes, NTUC, or community initiatives, such as M3+.

sections.label: HashTech programme in Pasir Ris-Changi
sections.summary: The HashTech programme in Pasir Ris-Changi introduces children to AI, robotics and autonomous systems, including activities such as Robot Wars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Through the HashTech programme in Pasir Ris–Changi, we are beginning to introduce our children to AI, robotics and autonomous systems – including through activities such as Robot Wars.

sections.label: AI for Malay culture and language
sections.summary: AI can help digitalise old Jawi manuscripts, produce batik designs from traditional Malay motifs, and facilitate Malay language learning and translation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: AI can assist in digitalising old Jawi manuscripts, producing batik designs inspired by traditional Malay motifs and facilitating the learning and translation of the Malay language.

sections.label: Renewing the social compact
sections.summary: The transition tests the social compact, which must be renewed so businesses, workers and Government move together and no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, at its heart, this is not just an economic transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is a test of our social compact, a compact that must now be renewed for a new era where businesses commit to not just profits but to people, where workers commit to not just jobs, but to lifelong growth, and where the Government continues to stand with both, ensuring that no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we can do this, if we can move forward together with trust, purpose and shared responsibility, this transformation will not divide us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It will make us stronger because when workers, businesses and the Government move together, we do not just adapt to change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We shape it, we benefit from it and we ensure that every Singaporean moves forward together.

sections.label: Workfare, Silver Support, Jobseeker Support
sections.summary: The passage states structural support exists through Workfare Income Supplement and Silver Support, and income relief for the involuntarily unemployed through SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is more structural or permanent social support in the form of the Workfare Income Supplement and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the Government, recognising the greater risk of economic and job disruption, has introduced income relief for the involuntarily unemployed through SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support, which has been discussed by Members of this House.

sections.label: AI and graduate hiring
sections.summary: The passage states job displacement depends on technology diffusion speed, and that employment rates for young degree holders have remained broadly stable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is because the extent of job disintermediation or displacement depends on the speed of technology diffusion, which has historically followed an S-curve.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I filed a Parliamentary Question in March asking whether MOM has detected any signs of AI prompting a slowdown in the hiring of fresh graduates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The response I received then, which was reaffirmed yesterday as well, was that employment rates for young degree holders has remained broadly stable.

sections.label: AI age profits to technology companies
sections.summary: The passage states a concern that in the AI age profits will accrue more to technology companies and shareholders and less to workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A related concern that many in this House have also discussed is that in the AI age, profits will increasingly accrue to technology companies and those who own shares in these companies, and less to workers as skills become commoditised.

sections.label: Singapore inclusive growth path
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's economic development has been a story of inclusive growth and that this path must continue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's economic development has been a story of inclusive growth – and that is the path we must stay on.

sections.label: Ownership of learning and career development
sections.summary: The passage states this means leaving comfort zones, taking on different tasks and diverse teams, and taking ownership of learning and career development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means getting out of our comfort zones, continuously challenging ourselves, getting used to different tasks and work environments, and working in diverse teams.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is everybody's responsibility: to take ownership of our own learning and career development, leveraging public funding and resources where available.

sections.label: Resident workforce with university degrees
sections.summary: The passage states that today over 40% of the resident workforce have university degrees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, over 40% of the resident workforce have university degrees.

sections.label: Job design on skills
sections.summary: Enterprises can centre job design on skills rather than credentials.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Enterprises can do so by centring job design on skills rather than credentials.

sections.label: Singapore skills-first employment practices
sections.summary: Singapore can set the pace in skills-first employment practices and human-centric job redesign, and the Institute for Adult Learning's Centre for Skills-First Practices launched working papers and roundtables.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore has the opportunity to set the pace in skills-first employment practices and human-centric job redesign, which will benefit both our firms and workers and is critical for our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute for Adult Learning’s Centre for Skills-First Practices recently launched a series of skills-first working papers and accompanying roundtable discussions.

sections.label: Adult learning research institutes
sections.summary: Several institutes have set up skills and adult learning initiatives, and the Institute for Adult Learning can serve as a national focal point for adult learning and employability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Management University has set up a Resilient Workforces Institute, while the Singapore Institute of Technology has launched a Skills Assessment and Validation initiative.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the Singapore University of Social Sciences, the Institute for Adult Learning has an Adult Learning Collaboratory and a Centre for Skills-First Practices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With end-to-end expertise from research to translation, the Institute for Adult Learning can serve as a national focal point for adult learning and employability.

sections.label: National AI and Tripartite Jobs Councils
sections.summary: The formation of the National AI Council and the Tripartite Jobs Council underscores this commitment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The formation of the National AI Council and the Tripartite Jobs Council underscores this commitment.

sections.label: Reaction to Singapore's AI priority
sections.summary: After being told Singapore's priority is equipping workers to work with and alongside AI, she described the contrast as stark and inspiring.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When I shared with her that Singapore’s priority is equipping workers to work with and alongside AI, she described the contrast, in her words, as "stark" and "inspiring".

sections.label: Survey on worker anxiety
sections.summary: An NTUC survey found over half of PMEs feel an urgent need to upskill, nearly a third are anxious about replacement, and other studies show half of Singaporeans fear automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: A recent NTUC survey found that more than half of our PMEs feel an urgent need to upskill just to stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Nearly a third are actively anxious about being replaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Other studies have shown that half of Singaporeans fear that their roles could be automated, and many are concerned that AI will benefit the bottom-lines of corporations more than it benefits the everyday worker.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and AI adoption
sections.summary: Singapore invested in lifelong learning through SkillsFuture, and the National AI Impact Programme aims to support 10,000 enterprises and 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For years, we have proactively anticipated a disruption like this, by investing and imbuing in Singaporeans the value of lifelong learning and the need to regularly upskill through programmes, such as SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This has put us in a good starting position as we push hard on AI adoption, like the National AI Impact Programme that aims to support 10,000 enterprises and help 100,000 workers become more AI fluent.

sections.label: National AI literacy programme
sections.summary: The speaker says a national AI literacy and fluency programme should be rolled out for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If embracing AI is a national strategic move, then we should roll out a national AI literacy and fluency programme for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Micron Singapore AI upskilling
sections.summary: Prof Er Meng Hwa cited Micron Singapore's in-house AI upskilling, which let employees use AI tools for insights, risks, tasks, projects and decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Prof Er Meng Hwa, in a recent Business Times article advocating for deeper learning, gave the example of Micron Singapore, whose in-house AI upskilling initiative did not stop at awareness but allowed employees to use AI tools to extract insights faster, analyse risks better, automate route tasks, plan projects more effectively and improve decision-making.

sections.label: AI National Council plans
sections.summary: The speaker is confident the AI National Council, led by the Prime Minister, will lay out plans on long-term advancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This Government has been deliberate in focusing our policies on long-term advancement rather than on short-term gains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am therefore confident that the AI National Council, led by the Prime Minister, will lay out plans and initiatives on the same basis.

sections.label: Market intelligence and foresight system
sections.summary: The speaker supports Mr Ng Chee Meng's proposal for a market intelligence and foresight system, and suggests using it to incentivise AI startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Before I conclude, I wish to support the proposal by NTUC Secretary-General, Mr Ng Chee Meng, for the setting up of a market intelligence and foresight system contextualised to the Singapore market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We can appreciate how useful it would be to draw insights from information, data points, analysis and the research of tripartite partners to sense-make for early signals, coordinate responses and provide proactive early intervention, where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: That said, while supporting our workers to retrain and move on to different roles to prevent displacement is important, we should also explore the possibility of using information from the same system to identify how the Government can incentivise AI startups to create new jobs and opportunities for our workforce.

sections.label: EDB expected jobs fall
sections.summary: EDB announced the expected number of jobs created fell to 15,700, the lowest in at least 20 years, despite more investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Economic Development Board (EDB) announced that the expected number of jobs to be created fell to 15,700, the lowest in at least 20 years, despite having attracted more investments than the year before.

sections.label: Fair retrenchment standards
sections.summary: Calls for higher retrenchment standards, including early notifications, union-negotiated benefits and AI grant conditions requiring redeployment efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As a start, we need to raise our standards for what constitutes fair and responsible retrenchment, such as by requiring early retrenchment notifications, supporting unions to negotiate for retrenchment benefits according to industry norms and designing AI grant incentives with conditions requiring employers to demonstrate efforts to meaningfully re-deploy workers whose roles and tasks are taken over by AI.

sections.label: Jobseeker Support income threshold
sections.summary: Notes the $5,000 income threshold covers under 20% of resident PMEs and suggests raising it to $8,400 or equivalent schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The income threshold for Jobseeker Support Scheme is currently set at $5,000 excluding CPF, which would only cover less than 20% of resident PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider raising this threshold to the gross median resident PME income, currently at $8,400 as of 2025, or consider some other suitable schemes of equivalence to address the needs of impacted PMEs.

sections.label: AI guessing personal characteristics
sections.summary: A joint SUTD-GovTech study found large learning models can reliably guess personal characteristics from other data points even in anonymised resumes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: A joint Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)-GovTech study found that large learning models can reliably guess personal characteristics, like gender of candidate from other data points like hobbies and volunteering, even when resumes are anonymised.

sections.label: Guidelines for employment-related AI
sections.summary: Proposes AI risk assessments, human oversight, HR training, worker awareness of AI use and redress, and baseline fairness from AI vendors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, that employers who adopt employment-related AI be guided to conduct risk assessments proportionate to the level of impact and ensure meaningful human oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, that HR professionals be supported with training and self-assessment tools to use AI responsibly and identify biasness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: They should know where AI is being used in decisions that affect them, what guardrails are in place and how existing avenues of redress apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And fourth, that we explore going upstream, working with AI vendors and developers to ensure that the underlying software meets some baseline principles of fairness and transparency before it reaches our workplaces.

sections.label: TTSH Smart Scheduler rollout
sections.summary: At TTSH, HSEU and management rolled out a Smart Scheduler cutting rostering time from over 90 minutes to under 15.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH), where our Healthcare Services Employees' Union (HSEU) worked with management through the CTC to roll out a Smart Scheduler that could handle multiple shift patterns and cut rostering time from more than 90 minutes to under 15, so that nurse managers could spend more time on other core work instead.

sections.label: Broadening Jobseeker Support eligibility
sections.summary: Suggests broadening Jobseeker Support eligibility criteria so more PMEs can benefit and have greater security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The eligibility criteria for Jobseeker Support assistance can be broadened, so that more PMEs can benefit and have greater security.

sections.label: AI transition fairness principles
sections.summary: AI is a once-in-a-generation technology that could concentrate gains and displace workers, so three principles must guide the AI transition.

sentences.text: AI's impact on the broad middle means that it is a "once-in-a-generation technology" but could also be a once-in-a-generation divider that concentrates gains to those who control AI while displacing the very same workers who helped to design, implement and build it.

These are three principles that must guide us in the way forward if we hope to anchor AI as an enabler in our AI transition in fairness, resilience and opportunities for all, because every worker matters.

sections.label: Fair deal for workers
sections.summary: Companies benefiting from Singapore and public resources supporting transformation are expected to deliver clear outcomes for workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Where companies benefit from operating and growing in Singapore, we will expect a fair deal for workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Where public resources and policies are used in support of business transformation, we expect companies to deliver clear and meaningful outcomes for workers.

sections.label: Targeted support for PMEs
sections.summary: The committee recognises PMEs may face greater job uncertainties and will recommend targeted support, including Jobseeker Support Scheme enhancements and private sector placement expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: On PMEs specifically, the committee recognises that they may face greater job uncertainties and will recommend more targeted support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: This includes considering enhancements to the Jobseeker Support Scheme, as Mr Patrick Tay suggested, and tapping on private sector expertise to strengthen placement support for this group.

sections.label: Raise floor widen door
sections.summary: The response is to raise the floor and widen the door.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Our response is to raise the floor and widen the door.

sections.label: AI courses and tools access
sections.summary: From the second half of 2026, IHLs will offer selected AI courses at discounts for alumni, and Singaporeans completing selected AI courses get six months of premium AI tools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: From the second half of 2026, all of our IHLs will offer selected AI-related courses at significant discounts for their alumni, for a period of one year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: For workers already in the workforce, Singaporeans who complete selected AI training courses will receive six months of complimentary access to premium AI tools.

sections.label: Redesigning jobs with workers
sections.summary: Jobs should be redesigned with workers so people work alongside AI, and redeployment and reskilling should be tried before retrenchment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: It also means redesigning jobs in close consultation with workers, as suggested by Ms Yeo Wan Ling, so that people can work alongside AI, using judgement, context and experience, rather than treating workers simply as a cost to be reduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: And where roles do change or disappear, it means making a serious effort to redeploy and reskill workers within the organisations before turning to retrenchment.

sections.label: Company reskilled redeployed 2000 workers
sections.summary: The company reskilled and redeployed more than 2,000 workers into higher-skilled roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: At the same time, the company reskilled and redeployed more than 2,000 workers into higher-skilled roles.

sections.label: Maxi-Cash reskills sales advisors AI
sections.summary: Maxi-Cash reskilled 25 sales advisors to use an AI-enabled authentication system that assesses jewellery composition in five seconds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Maxi-Cash enhanced this process by reskilling 25 of their sales advisors to use an AI-enabled authentication system, which can accurately assess the composition of jewellery in just five seconds.

sections.label: Sharing gains from growth fairly
sections.summary: The speaker says there is broad agreement that gains from growth and progress must be shared fairly and broadly with all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: That is the nature of democratic debate, and it is very healthy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: But I believe there is broad agreement across this House on a fundamental principle: that the gains from growth and progress must be shared fairly and broadly with all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Gains not only for capital holders
sections.summary: The gains must not accrue only to those who already have capital, advantages or access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: The gains must not accrue only to those who already have capital, advantages or access.

sections.label: Government on workers' side
sections.summary: The Government tells workers it is on their side and is acting before the disruption reaches them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: To workers watching this debate, I want to say this directly to you: the Government is on your side, and we are acting before the disruption reaches you, not after.

sections.label: Not every business needs AI
sections.summary: Not every business needs to adopt AI, and not every pursuit needs to be seen through AI transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Not every business needs to adopt AI, and not every pursuit needs to be seen through the lens of AI transformation.

sections.label: Reviewing education for AI age
sections.summary: The education system will be reviewed to develop these qualities with the same rigour applied to academic excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: In an AI age, they will become the hard edge of competitive advantage for our people and for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: That is why we will review our education system, to make sure we develop these qualities with the same rigour and intentionality we have always applied to academic excellence.

sections.label: Students who question and explore
sections.summary: A student who asks unexpected questions and pursues deep interests may be ahead, and this will be done with educators, parents and young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: A student who asks the unexpected questions, who pursues something deeply out of genuine interest, who can hold two contradictory ideas and work through them – that student is not behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: In the world that we are building, that student may be ahead of all of us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We are committed to doing this, together with our educators, our parents and young Singaporeans themselves.

sections.label: Workers facing economic disruption
sections.summary: No one should face disruption alone, and workers should move forward as the economy grows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Some will face real disruption and our responsibility is to ensure no one faces it alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: And we will ensure that as our economy grows, our workers move forward with it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: If we develop Singaporeans who are curious, creative and deeply human, people who can ask the questions that machines cannot and earn the trust that algorithms never will, then we will not merely manage this transition.

sections.label: Seniors' AI access and confidence
sections.summary: The issue is lack of access and confidence, not willingness, and MOM's 2025 report found residents aged 50 to 64 had the lowest training participation at 44.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This encouraged me because it shows that the issue is not a lack of willingness, but rather a lack of access and, to some extent, to some of them, it is about confidence, which we can overcome by curating and customising access to AI tools and making time for our seniors to learn and to increase their knowledge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We see a gap in training participation, where MOM's 2025 report found that residents aged 50 to 64 had the lowest training participation rate at 44.5%, compared with about 60% for those who are below 40 years old.

sections.label: Older adults' learning and AI use
sections.summary: OECD 2025 found learning-by-doing opportunities fall with age, and a Pew 2025 report found 73% of AI-using workers were aged 18 to 49.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: OECD's Employment Outlook 2025 highlights that across OECD countries, opportunities to learn by doing fall with age, where 62% of adults aged 25 to 29 reported such opportunities, but this falls to 45% among those who are 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In addition, a 2025 Pew Research Centre report found that 73% of workers who used AI at work were aged 18 to 49, while only 27% were aged 50 and above.

sections.label: Seniors enrolling in AI courses
sections.summary: Since February 2026, more than 4,000 workers enrolled in LearningHub's AI courses, and 39% of them are seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Since February 2026, more than 4,000 workers have enrolled in LearningHub's AI courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: I am also very happy that 39% of them are seniors.

sections.label: NTUC CTCs and transformation projects
sections.summary: NTUC has formed 3,800 CTCs, started over 900 business transformation projects and benefited over 300,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To date, NTUC has formed 3,800 CTCs, embarked on over 900 business transformation projects, benefiting over 300,000 workers.

sections.label: New system cuts manual work
sections.summary: The new system cut manual work like order processing by about 60%, letting the company handle 40% more orders and give wage increments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: With this new system, manual work such as order processing was reduced by about 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As they became more productive, the company could handle 40% more orders and provide wage increments for its employees.

sections.label: Tripartite solidarity and AI opportunities
sections.summary: Tripartite solidarity made firms more productive and workers better paid, and efforts will be built on so workers and enterprises seize AI opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Because tripartite partners moved together in solidarity, firms became more productive, workers took on better jobs with better pay and Singapore strengthened its competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: It will build on efforts across the Government, employers and the Labour Movement and enable partners to scale outreach, accelerate policy implementation and direct resources so that workers and enterprises can seize opportunities from AI.

sections.label: NTUC AI-Ready SG initiative
sections.summary: In February this year, NTUC launched the AI-Ready SG initiative to encourage workers to learn and master AI tools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In February this year, the NTUC launched the AI-Ready SG initiative, actively encouraging workers to learn and master AI tools.

sections.label: Upskilling to close gaps
sections.summary: The passage urges taking a step to upskill and learn, including from younger colleagues, to close access and skills gaps and expand opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Take that step with us, upskill and learn, including from your younger colleagues and together, we can close the access gap, narrow the skills gap and expand opportunities for all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Because in Singapore, we have always believed that progress must be inclusive, that as we move forward, we move forward together, because every worker matters.

sections.label: Surveys on AI-driven cuts
sections.summary: Global surveys show two in three companies that made earlier AI-driven cuts are rehiring, and a MOM study shows about 6% of Singapore firms reduced headcount due to AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Recent global surveys show that two in three companies that made earlier AI-driven cuts are already rehiring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the preparation for my speech today, my team used AI to help refine the work to me.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It surfaced useful references, including our MOM's newly released study showing only about 6% of firms in Singapore have reduced headcount due to AI adoption.

sections.label: National AI Equity Fund purpose
sections.summary: The National AI Equity Fund is not a compensation for failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: The National AI Equity Fund is not about a compensation for failure.

sections.label: Workers' share of AI gains
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government will ensure workers get a direct, tangible share of AI productivity gains beyond training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Can the Minister elaborate on how the Government intends to ensure workers receive a direct and tangible share of AI productivity gains beyond just more training?

sections.label: SWDA performance index outcomes
sections.summary: SWDA will have key performance index outcomes tying the Enterprise Workforce Training Package and job redesign to real wage and career progression improvements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For today's Motion, the NTUC Secretary-General will be wrapping up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But in the months, in the years ahead, I have shared that SWDA will have very clear key performance index outcomes, including tying the Enterprise Workforce Training Package, job redesign to specific skin in the game for both the businesses tapping on such grants, to improvement in real wages and career progression for the workers.

sections.label: AI grants and worker outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker asks what worker outcomes will be tracked and whether job redesign will be an explicit condition of AI grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: In my speech on job redesign, I had asked for AI grants to be tied to mandatory job redesign requirements and productivity gains linked to worker outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: And I am very glad to hear that the Ministry has set out expectations of companies that benefit from AI and a vision for good jobs in the AI age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: I am also very happy to hear that you have committed by saying that public support will come with worker outcome expectations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Would the Minister of State be able to share what specific worker outcomes will be tracked and whether job redesign will be an explicit condition of our AI grants, or simply an expectation that companies are just encouraged to meet?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: And what kind of mechanisms will you be putting in place to track and recognise companies that do this job redesign well?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: I think this is something that we should discuss together with all of our tripartite partners, whether it is with unions as well as business leaders, to make sure that any of our grant and support schemes do not end up making things even harder for companies that want to transform.

sections.label: 90-day notice commencement clarity
sections.summary: The Member is asked to clarify how companies, especially SMEs, determine when the 90-day notice formally commences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: The issue is therefore operational reality and definitional ambiguity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: So, could the Member clarify how companies, especially many of our SMEs, are expected to determine when this 90-day notice should formally commence?

sections.label: Four practical moves for AI
sections.summary: The speaker put forth four practical moves on market intelligence, enterprise transformation, worker opportunities and displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: In my opening, I put forth four practical moves: first, building market intelligence and foresight for an AI-enabled economy; second, enabling enterprises to transform with AI and to do so in a way that benefits workers; third, enabling workers to seize new opportunities; and fourth, enabling displaced workers to bounce back with dignity and confidence.

sections.label: NTUC Labour Alliance coLab research community
sections.summary: NTUC formed the Labour Alliance coLab, a research community with academics bringing together experts across IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Within NTUC, we have begun contributing to this work through our Labour Alliance co-laB (LAB), a research community we formed with academics that brings together experts across our IHLs.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council AI adoption
sections.summary: The Tripartite Jobs Council consolidates tripartite partners' capabilities, and the Government supported NTUC's proposal to form it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: He also suggested that trade associations and chambers could become platforms that accelerate AI adoption across sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This is exactly what the Tripartite Jobs Council is setting out to do – to consolidate tripartite partners' various capabilities under one roof to better serve out our enterprises and our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I am glad the Government has supported NTUC's proposal to form this Tripartite Jobs Council.

sections.label: Patrick Tay 3 Es proposals
sections.summary: Mr Patrick Tay called for the 3 Es and proposed raising Jobseeker Support eligibility to the PME median income and earlier retrenchment notification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: On the fourth move to enable displaced workers to bounce back with dignity and confidence, Mr Patrick Tay called on the "3 Es" – equitable growth, enhanced protections and engaged workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: He calls to raise the Jobseeker Support scheme eligibility to the PME median income – around $8,400 as of 2025 – and to provide earlier notification of retrenchment.

sections.label: Andre Low redundancy insurance proposal
sections.summary: Mr Andre Low questioned whether the JSS is sufficient and proposed a redundancy insurance scheme instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Mr Andre Low questioned whether the JSS is sufficient and proposed a redundancy insurance scheme instead.

sections.label: Tripartite partners innovate Workfare PWM JSS
sections.summary: The Government will work closely with tripartite partners to innovate, as done for Workfare, Progressive Wage Model and now the JSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We will work closely with tripartite partners to innovate, as we have done before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)

sections.label: Wage support and OJT design
sections.summary: The CTC grant lacks a six-month salary subsidy, and SMEs lack capacity for structured OJT, so expert consultants are proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: First is the depth of the wage support, and second is the structural design of OJT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: While the CTC grant can support training fees and process redesign, its primary lever still remains project-based capital expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: It does not provide the aggressive six-month salary subsidy required to derisk the transition for an employer when a worker's productivity temporarily drops because of intensive AI training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And many SMEs currently lack the internal capacity to design effective structured OJT, so my proposal provides the necessary, what we call, "design brains" through a dedicated pool of expert OJT consultants to ensure that the mastery that they achieve is both practical and is not just administrative.
